VibePascal v55 -- arm-linux NATIVE compiler (runs on 32-bit ARM Linux, e.g.
Raspberry Pi 32-bit OS).  -FU/-FE output directories are created instead of
aborting the build.
Source commit: eae5d3e919 (merge of fix/output-dir-autocreate)
Compiler fix:  4d10b26fe772dfbd4992cbeb53f09028f7dfee4f
Parent release: v54 (b7d2d9676ecf1d7d8250cd460b9c48069920513e)
Built: 2026-09-10, cross-built on x86_64-linux via compiler/ppcrossarm
Binary: bin/ppcarm  md5 494305fbcdbc4e156a7357fe0940d573

ABI: ARMHF -- ARM EABI5, HARD float (VFP).  This is the ABI of Raspberry Pi OS
32-bit and of Debian/Ubuntu armhf.  It is NOT compatible with an armel
(soft-float) system.  The compiler reports "Target OS: Linux for ARMHF".
The ABI attributes are byte-identical to the v54 binary and were re-read from
both this cycle, not quoted: Tag_CPU_arch v7, Tag_FP_arch VFPv3-D16,
Tag_ABI_VFP_args VFP registers.  D16 (not D32) is deliberate and confirmed
against BuildMaster's own arm component builds -- nothing about the float
tuning changed in v55.

COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  Only compiler/options.pas changed between v54 and v55:
no RTL change, no package change, no PPU format change, so the existing v54
arm-linux units tarball in this directory stays valid and is still the one to
pair with this binary.

WHAT CHANGED
  -FE and -FU name where the COMPILER writes.  Up to and including v54 a
  missing one was an error: -FE reported 'Path "x/" does not exist' during
  option processing, and -FU failed later and far more obscurely at object
  write time ("Can't create object file: x/hello.o (error code: 2)").  In both
  cases the compiler knew the path and made the user run mkdir.  v55 creates
  both directories up front, recursively.  An IMPOSSIBLE path still stops the
  build with the same message -- now reported only after creation has been
  TRIED and FAILED, so it arrives early and names the directory.

VERIFIED ON THIS TARGET, UNDER EMULATION (qemu-user, 2026-09-10)
  A/B against the PUBLISHED pre-fix v54 binary (md5
  da6167de452b8dfdb4f57e33ffb8c733), same source, same options, same fresh
  directory, varying ONLY the compiler.  11 corners; every "must compile"
  corner had its emitted ARM binary EXECUTED and required to print 42, not
  merely linked:

    BASELINE 4/11, FIXED 11/11.

    Fixed: -FU one level, -FU three levels, -FU absolute, -FU units/sub,
    -FE relative, -FU and -FE together, and an fpc.cfg carrying the shipped
    -FU./units/$FPCTARGET shape (v54: "Can't create object file:
    ./units/arm-linux/hello.o").
    Unchanged and still passing on both: -FU on an existing dir, no options.
    Unchanged and still REFUSING on both, non-zero and without an internal
    error: -FU under a plain file, -FU under a read-only dir.

  No semantic regression.  tinlinevarnativeint1 (NativeInt=4 on this 32-bit
  target), tinlinevarstrinfer1 and the cy1096 block-scope finalization matrix
  were compiled AND run under qemu by both the v54 and the v55 binary with
  identical verdicts, and both { %FAIL } scope tests are still correctly
  rejected by both.

WHAT THIS IS NOT
  qemu-user is an emulator, not a Raspberry Pi.  It runs the real shipped
  bytes and real ARM encodings, so codegen and RTL defects surface, but nobody
  has run any VibePascal ARM artifact on physical ARM silicon and this release
  does not change that.

REPRODUCE IT: dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh, which now selects the highest-
numbered tarball per target rather than a hardcoded version, and asserts the
-FU/-FE behaviour in a version-aware way (>= v55 must create the directory;
below v55 must refuse).
